title: Al-Hajjaj and the Three Young Scholars

keywords: al-hajjaj and the three young men
full_text:
The night watch of Basra arrested three young men walking through the streets after the strict curfew imposed by the fierce governor Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf. Brought before the governor’s tribunal at dawn, Al-Hajjaj glared at them with fury: 'Who are you, and what gives you the arrogance to defy my curfew? Identify your lineage before the executioner strikes!'

The first youth stepped forward and recited with bold poetic elegance:
'My father is one whose command the people obey,
Before his sharp blade their banners give way;
He holds up the world in the storm and the fight,
And nations submit to his courage and might!'
Al-Hajjaj thought: 'Surely, his father is a mighty general!' and held back his sword.

The second youth declaimed with equal majesty:
'My father is one who turns charcoal to gold,
Whose wisdom and skill through the cities are told;
The mighty bow down as he shapes the hot glow,
And kings seek the treasures his craft can bestow!'
Al-Hajjaj thought: 'His father must be the chief alchemist and jeweler of the realm!'

The third youth spoke with quiet, fearless dignity:
'My father is one whose high deeds are his own,
Who walks without fear and who stands all alone;
I boast of no lineage, I lean on no name,
For virtue and honor are my only claim!'

Al-Hajjaj investigated their parentage: the first youth’s father was a humble village barber; the second youth’s father was a common charcoal-burner; and the third youth was an orphan scholar!

Al-Hajjaj laughed aloud, his wrath completely conquered by their brilliant wit, poetic eloquence, and courageous presence of mind.

He declared: 'Learn from these youths! A man’s true lineage is the sharpness of his mind and the integrity of his character, not the dust of his ancestors!' The governor rewarded each with a hundred dinars and appointed them to the municipal academy.
moral: True nobility is earned through personal virtue, intellect, and courage, not mere ancestral pride.
